prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on your needs (budget, roof type, insurance claim, timeline), but here’s how to find the best roof replacement contractor in Dallas and next steps I can take for you.

What the best company will have
- Valid insurance (general liability + workers’ comp) and local registrations/permits. Ask to see certificates.  
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, etc.) — this enables extended warranties.  
- Strong local reputation and years in business in the Dallas area (familiar with local codes, storms).  
- High, recent reviews on Google/Yelp/BBB and verifiable references (ask for recent jobs).  
- Clear, itemized written estimate and a written workmanship warranty in addition to the shingle manufacturer warranty.  
- Uses full‑time crews (not just hired day labor), pulls permits, and handles municipal inspections.  
- Good communication, realistic timeline, and a clean-up plan (magnet sweep for nails).  

Red flags to avoid
- High-pressure sales tactics, door‑to‑door “storm chasers.”  
- Demand for large upfront cash payment (reasonable deposit only, often 10–30%).  
- No physical address or unverifiable references.  
- Vague contract or unwillingness to put materials/cleanup/warranty in writing.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed/registered to work in the City of Dallas? Can you provide COI (certificate of insurance)?  
- Are you a certified installer for these shingle brands? Which warranties will apply?  
- Who will perform the work (employees or subs)? Timeline? Start and completion dates?  
- What is included in the price (ice & water shield, drip edge, felt, ridge vents, flashing, gutters if applicable)?  
- How do you handle permitting and inspections? What is your cleanup guarantee?  
- Can you provide 3 recent local references and examples of recent storm‑damage jobs?

Practical next steps I can do for you
- If you give your Dallas zip code or neighborhood, I can compile a short list (3–5) of highly rated local roofers with recent reviews, certifications, and contact info.  
- Or I can draft an email/template estimate request and checklist you can send to contractors.

If you want recommendations, tell me your zip code, roof material (asphalt shingle, tile, metal), whether you’ll file an insurance claim, and any schedule or budget constraints. I’ll pull local options and a recommended shortlist.
